title: Provisioning Concierge: entitlement orchestration and autoscale gating
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement: current dedicated capacity onboarding mixes manual steps and ad-hoc approvals which causes long lead times and opaque guarantees for throughput. Customers expect clear entitlement artifacts (committed throughput and burst margins), deterministic autoscale gating rules, and a traceable approval path that ties to billing and SLA contracts.

Goal: design and deliver a "Provisioning Concierge" workflow that orchestrates reservation requests into validated entitlements, enforces autoscale gating at the fleet-level, and outputs machine-readable artifacts for billing, rollout and runtime enforcement. The Concierge should reduce mean provisioning time by >=40%, eliminate manual email approvals in 70% of cases, and provide a single source of truth (approval audit + capacity ledger).

Scope: request capture UX (console + API), automated preflight checks (quota, region, model compatibility), staged approvals (auto-approve, PO/finance check, security review), entitlement issuance (throughput tokens, burst window, SLO class), autoscale gate configuration (min/max, warm pools, scale-back policy), and post-approval onramp (scheduler allocation + capacity reservation). Integrations: billing, KMS for key access, Console dashboards, and the runtime's allocation API.

Success metrics: provisioning lead time median, percentage of auto-approved requests, accuracy of forecasted utilization vs actual within 15% at 7 days, and reduction in escalations to Solutions Eng.

Non-goals: full procurement/legal contract negotiation (we will hand off to Sales/contracts), changing the runtime allocation algorithms in this ticket (eng will consume the artifacts), or supporting air-gapped/on-prem flows in the first delivery.

Deliverables: PRD, console request form prototype, approval engine ruleset, entitlement JSON schema, billing mapping, and an ops runbook for escalations and rollback.
